# CPDataKit v0.10.1

This maintenance release fixes data integrity and local-workbench boundaries found during
synthetic round-trip and user-workflow review. It retains the general scientific/engineering
scope, Python >=3.12 and existing runtime dependencies.

CSV/JSON integers with missing values keep their precision. Identity/equivalent unit mappings
retain numeric storage types; unsafe integer promotion, overflow and nonzero underflow stop with
an actionable error. Tabular and scientific-array mappings share these checks.

HDF5 readers inspect container dependencies before payload access. External links, external raw
storage, virtual datasets and soft links are rejected; internal hard links remain supported.
This applies to native v1/v2, inspection, DAMASK and HDF5-backed NetCDF paths.

Uploads enforce cumulative file/request budgets before the entire multipart body can be spooled.
Session and header tokens are checked early; form-token fallback remains bounded. Separate
workspaces no longer overwrite each other's browser cookie when served on different local ports.

Conversion artifacts retain original CSV declarations, excluded columns, source digests and
ordered processing receipts across further conversions. The optional versioned lineage is bounded
and checksummed; old files remain readable with unknown historical completeness. These checks
detect inconsistent receipts, not an adversary who rewrites all hashes.

HDF5 record and materialization limits are checked before payload reads. Read checkpoints support
cooperative cancellation, and reporting reuses loaded data instead of repeatedly scanning it.
Simple variable-length strings use a conservative file-size/count estimate so small text tables
remain usable. Other variable-length payloads are rejected when their memory use cannot be
estimated safely; the ordinary unbounded API remains available for trusted inputs.

Windows native NetCDF3 input works from Unicode paths using a streamed, temporary ASCII snapshot.
The source is not rewritten, and the snapshot is cleaned up on success, rejection or cancellation.
Date coordinates can be read; a general datetime schema/normalization feature is not added.

The package README links directly to files in this release, and capability discovery no longer
claims CSV/JSON data export is implemented. Original CSV download remains byte-preserving.

Compatibility notes: ordinary inferred CSV still interprets leading zeros and default missing
tokens; use explicit CSV confirmation/string declarations for lexical identifiers. Inputs that
previously produced rounded data or depended implicitly on other HDF5 files now fail explicitly.
No cloud service, training system, new adapter family or runtime dependency was introduced.

See the [CSV walkthrough](https://github.com/koocmitwho/cpdatakit/blob/v0.10.1/examples/csv-intake/README.md)
and [verification record](https://github.com/koocmitwho/cpdatakit/blob/v0.10.1/docs/verification/2026-10-02-v0101.md).
